title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: customer-managed keys for direct export (Worldwide)
summary: The actionable guidance is supported, including request-only enablement, licensing prerequisites and export protection. Remove the unsupported statement that the feature adds no agent or automated action; two minor corrections concern the PowerShell wording and the citation for Key Vault charges.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans customer-managed key protection for Microsoft Purview eDiscovery direct export.
claims.quote: This release of eDiscovery features the implementation of customer-managed key (CMK) options, allowing users to manage their own encryption keys for the data included in the direct export workflow in eDiscovery

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: CMK direct export is admin-opt-in through a request, so existing tenants do not receive it merely by doing nothing.
claims.quote: Only enabled for specific tenants by request to Microsoft Support

claims.claim: Tenant enablement requires contacting Microsoft Support or a Customer Success Account Manager.
claims.quote: To enable this feature, contact Microsoft Support or your Customer Success Account Manager (CSAM) and request CMK for eDiscovery direct exports for your tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: When enabled, CMK protects exported investigation data at rest.
claims.quote: When enabled, exported investigation data is encrypted at rest using tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.

claims.claim: The encryption uses tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.
claims.quote: using tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.

claims.claim: This feature extends protection for tenants with Customer Key configured through MDEP.
claims.quote: Organizations that configure Customer Key through the Microsoft 365 Data-at-Rest Encryption Platform (MDEP) with a Data Encryption Policy (DEP) in policy assigned status can extend CMK protections to eDiscovery direct export packages.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].governs; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A DEP in PolicyAssigned state via MDEP onboarding cmdlets is a prerequisite.
claims.quote: A Data Encryption Policy (DEP) is in PolicyAssigned state via the Microsoft 365 Data-at-Rest Encryption Platform (MDEP) onboarding cmdlets.

claims.claim: Azure Key Vault must be configured following the standard Customer Key setup process.
claims.quote: Your organization configured Azure Key Vault following the standard Customer Key setup process.

claims.claim: The Learn documentation labels CMK for direct exports as preview.
claims.quote: Enable CMK (Customer Managed Key) for direct exports (preview)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Review set data at rest is not included in this protection.
claims.quote: This encryption applies to direct exports only. Data at rest in an eDiscovery review set isn't included at this time.

claims.claim: The service dynamically validates CMK configuration through MDEP at export time.
claims.quote: CMK configuration is dynamically validated through MDEP at export time.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: CMK direct export does not change the eDiscovery user experience.
claims.quote: No change to the eDiscovery user experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Direct export proceeds without CMK encryption if CMK is not properly configured through MDEP at export time.
claims.quote: If your tenant does not have CMK properly configured through MDEP at export time, direct export jobs will proceed without CMK encryption.

claims.claim: No new toggle is introduced; existing DEPs govern the behaviour.
claims.quote: Behavior is governed by existing Data Encryption Policies; no new toggle is introduced, but encryption is controlled through CMK configuration.

claims.claim: MC1289726 was updated on 14 August 2026.

claims.claim: The previous general availability rollout window was early to end of September.
claims.quote: late December 2026 (previously early September) and expect to complete by early January 2027 (previously end of September).

claims.claim: The service automatically manages encryption scopes, storage accounts and containers without additional storage configuration.
claims.quote: Encryption scopes, storage accounts, and containers are managed automatically by the service; no additional storage configuration is needed.

claims.claim: CMK does not change the 14-day exported-data retention period.

claims.claim: Search export packages expire 14 days after creation.
claims.quote: Search export packages expire 14 days after you create the export.

claims.claim: Expired search exports and their packaged data are deleted and cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: After 14 days, the export and all data contained in the export package are automatically deleted and can't be recovered.

claims.claim: Customer Key setup requires two paid Azure subscriptions.
claims.quote: Azure subscriptions: Two paid Azure subscriptions (Free, Trial, Sponsorship, MSDN, or Legacy Support aren't eligible)

claims.claim: Customer Key setup and multi-workload DEP assignment require Exchange admin permissions.
claims.quote: Permissions: Exchange admin permissions (all DEP operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell)

claims.claim: Customer Key administration places the two keys in separate Azure subscriptions under the organisation's administration.
claims.quote: As a best practice, have different members of your organization manage one key in each subscription. These subscriptions should be used only to administer encryption keys for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The Customer Key pages say all Customer Key operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Permissions: Exchange admin permissions (all Customer Key operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell)
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'Multi-workload DEP assignment uses Exchange Online PowerShell and requires Exchange admin permissions.' The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/customer-key-manage also says 'To configure Customer Key for SharePoint and OneDrive, use SharePoint PowerShell' and lists Azure PowerShell for Key Vault operations.

claims.claim: Each user benefiting from Customer Key requires a licence.
claims.quote: Each user who benefits from Customer Key requires a license. Requirements vary by workload.

claims.claim: For multiple workloads, the Customer Key licence count must cover the greater of the Exchange-licensed and Teams-licensed user counts.
claims.quote: Because data encryption policies apply at the tenant level, your tenant must have at least as many Customer Key licenses as users assigned Exchange or Teams licenses—whichever is greater.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Exporting content requires assigning the eDiscovery user a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 licence.
claims.quote: To export content in eDiscovery, assign the eDiscovery user a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: When exporting SharePoint content, the account also needs a Microsoft SharePoint E3 licence or SharePoint items might not export as expected.
claims.quote: When exporting SharePoint content, the account must also have a Microsoft SharePoint E3 license; otherwise, SharePoint items might not export as expected.

claims.claim: The Microsoft pages reviewed publish no separate charge specific to CMK on direct export.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery direct export customer managed key price licensing meter'; opened edisc-search-export, customer-key-set-up and the Purview service description; reviewed the edisc-billing search excerpt. No separate CMK direct-export charge was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No licence specific to CMK direct export is named beyond the documented prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery direct export customer managed key price licensing meter'; opened edisc-search-export, customer-key-set-up and the Purview service description; read MC1289726. No separate CMK direct-export SKU appeared.

claims.claim: The tenant remains responsible for Azure Key Vault usage charges under its paid Azure subscriptions.
claims.quote: 'purge' and 'recover' actions will count towards normal key vault operations and will be billed.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/key-vault/general/soft-delete-overview#scenarios to sources and cite it for the statement that Azure Key Vault usage is billed.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no self-service admin UI or API for enabling CMK direct export for a tenant.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK direct export PowerShell enable' and 'eDiscovery CMK direct export Microsoft Graph security settings enable customer managed key'; opened edisc-search-export and customer-key-manage; read MC1289726. Enablement requires Microsoft Support.

claims.claim: No admin UI for assigning the tenant's multi-workload DEP is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'multi-workload data encryption policy assignment admin portal UI'; opened customer-key-manage and customer-key-set-up. Assignment is documented through Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment, not a portal control.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID> assigns the tenant's multi-workload DEP, rather than reading its status.
claims.quote:
After creating a multi-workload data encryption policy (DEP), assign it using the Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment cmdlet.
Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID>

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The eDiscovery export page does not specify which DEP type satisfies its PolicyAssigned prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery direct export MDEP PolicyAssigned multi-workload DEP type'; opened edisc-search-export and customer-key-manage. The export page requires a DEP in PolicyAssigned state through MDEP onboarding cmdlets but does not name a DEP type.

claims.claim: Rolling back Customer Key for multiple workloads requires a Microsoft Support request.
claims.quote: If you no longer want to use Customer Key with multi-workload data encryption policies (DEPs), submit a support request through Microsoft Support.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how an administrator can see in the export report or portal whether an individual direct export used CMK.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery export report CMK encryption status settings.csv'; opened edisc-search-export and edisc-process-report-use, searched their text for CMK and encryption, and read the export-report search excerpts. No per-export CMK indicator was documented.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Encryption is applied automatically by the service based on the existing DEP configuration.
claims.quote: Encryption is applied automatically based on existing DEP configuration.

claims.claim: The tenant must remain CMK enabled at export time.
claims.quote: Your tenant must remain CMK enabled at the time of the export.

claims.claim: The protected at-rest copy of exported investigation data is held in eDiscovery storage accounts.
claims.quote: Exported investigation data is stored in eDiscovery storage accounts encrypted with customer-managed keys rather than Microsoft-managed keys.

claims.claim: The feature adds no agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK direct export adds agent automatic actions'; opened edisc-search-export and read MC1289726. These describe automatic encryption, not an assurance that no agent or automated action is added.
claims.fix: Remove 'No change: the feature adds no agent or automated action.' Retain 'Encryption is applied by the service during the export.'
